 Indonesia prepares for drought as El Niño delays rainy season
 Indonesia prepares for drought as El Niño delays rainy season
 October 25, 2026 / 10:07 AM 
 Share 
 Sharjah24 - AFP: Indonesia’s National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) is preparing measures to address the risk of prolonged drought, as El Niño could delay the onset of the rainy season until early 2027.
 BNPB official Berton Panjaitan said the agency continues to monitor and assess updated weather data from the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), according to Indonesian news agency ANTARA.
 The agency, ministries and local governments are developing daily and weekly measures to control drought and forest and land fires. Measures include "weather modification operations to increase the potential for rainfall by seeding NaCl and similar materials," Panjaitan said.
Central Java and Yogyakarta endured 131 days without rain, more than four months.
The BMKG said El Niño influenced the conditions. "We will continue to evaluate preparedness and mitigation, including determining the next step going forward," Panjaitan said.
BMKG Head Teuku Faisal Fathani earlier said the Pacific sea surface temperature anomaly hit +2.63 degrees, a very strong El Niño projected to last until early 2027.
BMKG forecasts a delayed rainy season start in most of Indonesia, covering 529 seasonal zones (ZOM), or 61.08% of Indonesia's land area.
The rains should arrive gradually from November 2026 in 185 ZOMs (24.66%) and December in 266 ZOMs (17.31%).
Accumulated rainfall in 510 ZOMs (69.76%) is predicted to remain normal despite the delayed start.
 The rainy season is forecast to peak at different times across Indonesia’s seasonal zones (ZOMs): in December 2026 in 155 zones (36.94%), January 2027 in 162 zones (25.68%) and February 2027 in 190 zones (16.79%).
BMKG also expects a shorter-than-usual rainy season in 482 zones.
